headline: CRUDE DROPS 5%; HARVEST PRESSURE BUILDS IN CORN
lead: Crude oil fell hard Friday, its biggest single-session drop in weeks, as Saudi ship-to-ship transfer reports quelled export-disruption fears that had been bid into the market all month. WTI settled at $95.78, down $5.34 on the session. Corn held at $5.31 while basis season begins its predictable grind lower toward the mid-October harvest low.
teaser: Crude's biggest drop in weeks resets the energy story; corn basis is starting its seasonal slide.

one_number.unit: average corn basis harvest-low vs. late-November
one_number.context: FarmDoc research published Friday: corn basis bottoms mid-October at harvest peak, averaging 11 cents under late-November levels. State-level lows reach 16 cents, deepest in Missouri.

yesterdays_call.note: Miss; beans slipped to $13.08, a nickel below $13.42, and the export-sales catalyst didn't hold the line.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called soybeans up toward $13.42 ($13.2625 when the call was made). It closed at $13.08.

action: Unpriced new-crop corn: a close under $5.28 is the next decision point. Do not wait for harvest-low basis to eat the margin.

sections.title: CRUDE LEADS LOWER
sections.body: - WTI fell to **$95.78**, its sharpest single-session drop in weeks, after Saudi ship-to-ship transfer reports eased fears the pipeline outage would cut export flow; the Iran-Hormuz cycle, a pattern of escalation and deflation running since July, just deflated again.
sections.so_what: Saudi route fears priced in; now they're priced out. Watch the next headline.

sections.title: GRAINS MIXED AT HARVEST DOOR
sections.body: - Corn held at **$5.31**, essentially flat, but the FarmDoc basis data in today's One Number is the real story: the price held; the basis is about to do the damage.
sections.so_what: Corn held the price; basis is about to do the damage. Time the sales accordingly.

sections.title: CATTLE AND HOGS DRIFT
sections.body: - Live cattle settled at **$216.20**, off 1.1%, and feeders fell to $334.95 at the same rate; the Cargill multi-plant lockout, ongoing since May 19, still holds roughly 6,000 head of daily processing capacity offline, keeping the packer-margin constraint in place.
sections.so_what: Cattle weakness is packer-driven, not supply-driven. The reopening pace is the next variable.

outside_the_pit.title: Senate Ag Advances Farm Bill 12-11 on Party Lines
outside_the_pit.body: The Senate Agriculture Committee voted Friday to send the farm bill to the full Senate, all Republicans in favor, all Democrats opposed.

watch_list.desc: Crop Progress; corn harvest pace above 15% signals normal flow, below 10% adds weather-delay premium.
Export Sales; soybeans under 300K MT keeps the chart, not demand, in charge of the move.
Saudi ship-to-ship transfer news; any disruption report puts $95.78 crude back in play immediately.

daily_quote.text: Perfection is achieved, not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away.

source_summary: CME Group settlement prices; USDA NASS; FarmDoc Daily (Illinois); OilPrice.com; FencePost; Feedstuffs; AGSIST locked price table 2026-09-18.
